summary: Reproduced Glm47MoeDetector non-streaming tool_index values following request tool-list positions ([0,0,0] and [0,1,0]) instead of response call order. Updated only the GLM-4.7/GLM-5 non-streaming path to assign dense local call indices, matching its streaming path, and added regression and skipped-unknown-tool boundary coverage.

tests.what_was_measured: Before the fix, actual Glm47MoeDetector.detect_and_parse returned indices [0,0,0] for three get_weather calls and [0,1,0] for get_weather/search/get_weather; raw output: reports/j-839dfae640d5/raw/reproduction-before.txt

Reported duplicate and mixed call sequences now produce [0,1,2]; a skipped unknown tool leaves the first emitted valid call at index 0; existing non-streaming and streaming multi-call behavior remains valid. 4 passed and 2 subtests passed.
Full GLM-4.7 detector unit class: 14 passed and 2 subtests passed; raw output: reports/j-839dfae640d5/raw/glm47-class-after.txt

gpu_execution_evidence: The defect and correction are deterministic CPU-side parsing of an already generated tool-call string. No model execution, numerical kernel, or GPU-dependent path is involved.
remaining_limitations: No GLM-4.7/GLM-5 model weights were available or needed, so no full model generation or HTTP serving reproduction was claimed.
The similarly structured detectors named in the issue scope note were not changed or qualified; this fix is intentionally limited to Glm47MoeDetector.
